Package: rurl
Type: Package
Title: Parse, Clean, and Normalize URLs
Version: 3.1.0.9000
Language: en-US
Authors@R:
    person("Bart", "Turczynski", email = "<email>", role = c("aut", "cre", "cph"),
           comment = c(ORCID = "0000-0002-8788-7980"))
Description: A lightweight toolkit for extracting structured information from URLs.
    Includes functions for parsing, normalizing protocols, extracting domains, and constructing clean URLs.
    Domain and public-suffix extraction is delegated to the 'pslr' package,
    which implements the Public Suffix List from <https://publicsuffix.org>.
    Punycode and IDNA encoding is handled by the 'punycoder' package,
    and IP address facts by the 'raddr' package.

# GitLab CI — the server-side gate.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. Every gate this repository owns ran in one place, GitHub
# Actions, and when `origin` moved to GitLab none of them ran anywhere. The local
# pre-push hook was the only enforcement left, and a hook is opt-in per clone
# (`pre-commit install`) — so "the history is green" meant nothing about whether
# anything had checked it.
#
# THE JOB LIST IS NOT WRITTEN HERE, DELIBERATELY. The `gates` and `check` jobs
# below shell out to `tools/verify.R`, which derives the gate list from
# `tools/verify-manifest.yml` at run time. Transcribing the gates into this
# file would create exactly the drift that script exists to prevent: add a
# gate to the manifest and a hand-maintained copy is silently incomplete from
# that moment. The manifest therefore stays the single source of truth for
# WHAT the gates are, regardless of which forge runs them -- it is
# forge-neutral (RURL-vunvxusf moved it out of `.github/workflows/`), and this
# file consumes it by running the script, never by copying it.
#
# WHAT RUNS WHEN (the fleet standard, seor design/fleet-standard.md):
#   every pipeline the `workflow:` block admits (a push to `main`, a tag, a
#   hand-started pipeline, a schedule):
#     gates            -- `tools/verify.R --gates` and the news-version gate.
#     citation-version -- CITATION.cff/.zenodo.json and the BugReports split.
#     check            -- `tools/verify.R`, the whole local gate: the gates,
#                         lint, spelling, `R CMD check --as-cran` through
#                         rcmdcheck, failing on a WARNING, and the test
#                         suite under LC_ALL=C. Not its docs stage, which
#                         `docs-drift` runs.
#     docs-drift       -- man/, NAMESPACE and DESCRIPTION against the pinned
#                         roxygen2.
#     coverage         -- covr: the badge regex, a cobertura report, and a
#                         failure below 95%.
#   `main` only:
#     pages            -- the pkgdown site, once `check` has passed.
#     fossa            -- `fossa analyze` (push only), the FOSSA scan.
#   the `deep-check` schedule only:
#     full-check       -- R release, oldrel and devel on rocker/r-ver.
#     floor-check      -- the declared R floor, from a dated snapshot.
#   the `dependency-audit` schedule only:
#     osv-audit, security-audit.
#
# `check` and `pages` used to run only on a tag or a hand-started pipeline,
# because GitLab.com's shared-runner minutes ran out (RURL-psqmlgjf). The fleet
# now runs on its own self-hosted runners (seor
# design/adr/0003-fleet-ci-runs-on-self-hosted-runners.md), and the fleet
# standard puts `R CMD check --as-cran`, coverage and the Pages deploy on every
# push to `main`.
#
# NOT COVERED HERE, so nobody reads a green pipeline as more than it is: the
# cross-platform matrix, rhub and the determinism matrix. Their GitHub
# workflows were deleted (RURL-vunvxusf); the determinism matrix is kept as a
# record under `tools/determinism/gha/`, and none of them runs anywhere.

# Before pushing a change to this file, run `glab ci lint .gitlab-ci.yml`. An
# unquoted `key: value` inside a script entry makes YAML read the `: ` as a
# mapping and GitLab rejects the whole config, creating ZERO jobs — which
# surfaces in the REST API as a bare "failed" pipeline with `yaml_errors: null`
# and no failure reason. Only GraphQL `failureReason` names it.

# PAUSED 2026-08-08 (RURL-psqmlgjf), RE-ENABLED 2026-09-03 (RURL-utsbwfvc).
# The pause was for GitLab.com's free-tier compute allowance, which no longer
# limits this project: every job runs on the fleet's self-hosted runners
# (`tags: [local-docker]` under `default:` below; SEOR-gpafxhua,
# SEOR-hhtzaknn). The `workflow:` block below limits how many pipelines fire,
# not compute (SEOR-bmgkzhvy).
#
# `tools/local-ci.sh` still runs these jobs in this image against a clean clone
# on demand (`--all origin/main` after a merge); it is the pull-based fallback,
# not a replacement for the per-push server-side run.

# ONE PIPELINE PER MERGE, NOT THREE (SEOR-bmgkzhvy). A branch pipeline and a
# merge-request pipeline used to fire alongside the pipeline on `main` for
# every slice -- three pipelines testing at most two distinct trees, on a
# fleet whose CI runs on self-hosted Docker runners on one Mac, not GitLab.com
# shared runners: `concurrent = 4` in `~/.gitlab-runner/config.toml`, a number
# this fleet owns and can change, not a platform limit (SEOR-gpafxhua;
# verified live and recorded in seor's
# design/adr/0003-fleet-ci-runs-on-self-hosted-runners.md). The branch
# pipeline is worse than redundant: the standing slice flow (agent-workflow skill)
# deletes the branch at merge before the runner starts it, so it dies at
# `get_sources` with exit 128 and leaves a red mark that represents nothing.
# The merge-request pipeline is worse than that: it can outlive its own MR and
# hold the runner's only slot for a full check run, blocking the `main`
# pipeline that actually matters. Neither pipeline ever gated a merge here --
# `only_allow_merge_if_pipeline_succeeds` is false on this project, and `main`
# is a protected branch (Maintainer-only push/merge) regardless of CI status --
# so dropping both costs no verification.
#
# COST, STATED PLAINLY: a feature-branch push now gets no CI at all, and
# neither does an API-triggered pipeline started against a non-default branch
# -- both fall through to the final `when: never` below. rurl had no job keyed
# on `merge_request_event` before this change, so no job's own `rules:` needed
# to move -- only which pushes get a pipeline at all changed.
#
# THE ONE EXCEPTION is a `web` pipeline, i.e. one a human started from Build >
# Pipelines > Run pipeline against a ref of their choosing. That is the escape
# hatch for getting a server-side answer about a branch BEFORE merging it, and
# it is safe to admit precisely because it cannot fire on its own: the problem
# above was entirely push- and merge-request-driven. It reaches `gates`,
# `citation-version` and `check`; `pages` is pinned to the default branch, so
# the hatch can verify a branch but never publish one (SEOR-bmgkzhvy).
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
      when: never
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web"
    - when: never

stages:
  - gates
  - check
  - deploy
  - audit

# Every job names the runner pool it depends on: the fleet's self-hosted
# Docker runners all carry `local-docker` (with run_untagged still true), so a
# job never falls back to a GitLab.com shared runner (SEOR-hhtzaknn).
default:
  image: r-base:latest
  interruptible: true
  tags: [local-docker]

# Debian's r-cran-* packages install in about a second; install.packages() would
# compile and cost minutes. Only what the gates actually need.
.gate_deps: &gate_deps
  - apt-get update -qq
  - apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends r-cran-yaml r-cran-digest r-cran-jsonlite

# The check stage needs the package's real dependency tree. Everything except
# the two siblings ships as a Debian binary, so this stays apt-fast instead of
# compiling stringi from source. Verified present in r-base:latest, not assumed.
#
# THE ASSERTION AT THE END IS LOAD-BEARING, so do not drop it as belt-and-braces.
# `install.packages()` reports a failed install as a WARNING and exits 0. The
# first run of this stage therefore installed NOTHING, exited clean, and let
# verify.R run against an empty library -- which reported three failures
# (lintr, R CMD build, testthat) that had nothing to do with the code. The
# job must die where the dependency is missing, not later wearing the costume
# of a product defect.
#
# knitr and rmarkdown were absent from the original list entirely, which is its
# own lesson: DESCRIPTION declares `VignetteBuilder: knitr`, and `R CMD build`
# re-renders both vignettes, so the build cannot even start without them.
.check_deps: &check_deps
  - apt-get update -qq
  - 'apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends
     r-cran-yaml r-cran-digest r-cran-jsonlite r-cran-curl r-cran-stringi
     r-cran-testthat r-cran-pkgload r-cran-lintr r-cran-rcmdcheck
     r-cran-knitr r-cran-rmarkdown r-cran-pkgdown r-cran-withr r-cran-spelling
     r-cran-rcpp pandoc qpdf'
  # hunspell from CRAN, over the r-cran-hunspell that r-cran-spelling pulls in
  # (RURL-czvqosis). Debian's build is +dfsg: it drops the bundled dictionaries
  # and reads the system en_US.aff, whose `WORDCHARS 0123456789` keeps digits
  # inside a token -- so "PV1" and "sha256" were checked whole here but as "PV"
  # and "sha" everywhere else, and 61 words passed locally and failed here. The
  # CRAN build ships the dictionaries every other machine checks against, and
  # installs into /usr/local/lib/R/site-library, which comes first on
  # .libPaths(). A failed install leaves Debian's build and the spelling step
  # red, never green by accident. r-cran-rcpp above spares compiling Rcpp.
  - 'Rscript -e ''install.packages("hunspell")'''
  # Not packaged by Debian, all on CRAN. oysteR and rosv are audit-only tools
  # that nothing here calls -- but `R CMD check` treats a missing Suggests as an
  # ERROR ("the suggested packages are required for a complete check"), and they
  # cost 27s together. Installing them keeps the check at full strength, which
  # is worth more than the seconds saved by _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false.
  # rlang and vctrs are named although Debian ships them: raddr needs rlang
  # >= 1.1.7 and vctrs >= 0.7.0, and install.packages() does not upgrade an
  # installed dependency that is too old, so the CRAN copies must be asked for.
  - 'Rscript -e ''install.packages(c("rlang", "vctrs", "raddr", "punycoder", "pslr", "oysteR", "rosv"))'''
  # DERIVED FROM DESCRIPTION, not transcribed -- same reason the gate list is.
  # A hand-copied dependency list is one more thing to forget: add a Suggests
  # and `R CMD check` starts ERRORing in CI with a hand-copy that is silently
  # incomplete from that moment. Reading Imports + Suggests means a new
  # dependency fails here, loudly, NAMING itself -- which tells whoever added it
  # exactly what to put in the apt line above (the only half that must stay
  # hand-written, because Debian's package names are not derivable from CRAN's).
  #
  # The version-bound stripper is spelled "[(].*" rather than an escaped paren
  # on purpose: a backslash here crosses YAML *and* the shell before R sees it,
  # and loses a level on the way. A character class needs no escaping in any of
  # the three.
  - 'Rscript -e ''d <- read.dcf("DESCRIPTION", c("Imports", "Suggests")); p <- trimws(sub("[(].*", "", unlist(strsplit(d[!is.na(d)], ",")))); p <- unique(c(p[nzchar(p)], "pkgload", "lintr", "rcmdcheck", "spelling")); m <- p[!vapply(p, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]; if (length(m)) stop("missing dependencies: ", paste(m, collapse = ", ")); cat("all", length(p), "dependencies present\n")'''

# pandoc is PINNED in every job that runs R, as the fleet standard requires
# (seor design/fleet-standard.md, "CI on every push to `main`"; SEOR-egfbijyi,
# SEOR-dpjdwhbi). Its markdown writer reflows text and pads tables differently
# between versions, so README.md is byte-stable only under the pandoc that knit
# it, and the vignettes and the pkgdown site render with it too. `gates`,
# `check`, `coverage`, `pages` and `full-check` splice this list into their
# script AFTER their apt install, never before it: r-base:latest's Debian
# pandoc is 3.11 (2026-10-04), and installing it after the pin would fail on
# the hold below (it would replace the pin without one). `dpkg -i` downgrades
# over it cleanly.
#
# AN ANCHORED LIST, NOT A TEMPLATE, and the pin a shell assignment, not a
# `variables:` entry: tools/local-ci-plan.R follows neither `extends:` nor
# `variables:`, so either would leave a local run on an unpinned pandoc. A
# plain anchor also suits the pre-commit `check-yaml` hook, which cannot
# construct GitLab's `!reference` tag. scripts/check-toolchain.R reads the
# PANDOC_VERSION line below and fails the pre-push gate when the local pandoc
# differs; seor's scripts/check-fleet-standard.py checks it against the
# fleet's version. A bump moves these together, in one change: this
# PANDOC_VERSION, both sha256 digests (the release's own published values),
# and README.md, re-knit under the new pandoc.
#
# r-base has no curl, hence the apt line. A failed or mismatched download
# only warns, and the job then runs on whatever pandoc it has: Debian's, from
# `.check_deps`, or none in `gates`, which renders nothing. Nothing unverified
# is ever installed. The download retries and has a ceiling: --max-time bounds
# each attempt and --retry-max-time the retries, so a stalled CDN reaches the
# warning in minutes instead of hanging the job. The architecture comes from
# `dpkg --print-architecture`, because the runner is arm64.
.pandoc_install: &pandoc_install
  - PANDOC_VERSION="3.10"
  - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates
  # `apt-mark hold pandoc`, only after a successful `dpkg -i`: no later apt
  # step replaces the pin. An upgrade leaves it, and an install that needs
  # another pandoc fails loudly. Where apt's pandoc is older than the pin, as
  # on rocker images, apt would not replace it anyway; the hold is the fleet's
  # canonical shape. A failed hold only warns, so it never stops a gate (seor
  # design/fleet-standard.md; SEOR-vzupmeqj).
  - |
    ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture)
    case "$ARCH" in
      amd64) PANDOC_SHA256=d502599878eb29af3ae5f0cb5d559134df96534125d452c7a0674a5bad2c5ecf ;;
      arm64) PANDOC_SHA256=b651c8bfd5a0a2f6650d6c0830131747ef67a1d9c0475b1399626611419e2205 ;;
      *) PANDOC_SHA256=unknown ;;
    esac
    if curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --retry-max-time 300 --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 120 \
      -o /tmp/pandoc.deb "https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/download/${PANDOC_VERSION}/pandoc-${PANDOC_VERSION}-1-${ARCH}.deb" \
      && echo "${PANDOC_SHA256}  /tmp/pandoc.deb" | sha256sum -c - \
      && dpkg -i /tmp/pandoc.deb; then
      apt-mark hold pandoc || echo "WARNING: pandoc ${PANDOC_VERSION} installed but not held; a later apt step may replace it"
      echo "pandoc ${PANDOC_VERSION} installed"
    else
      echo "WARNING: pandoc ${PANDOC_VERSION} not installed; this job runs on the image's or Debian's pandoc"
    fi
    if command -v pandoc >/dev/null 2>&1; then pandoc --version | sed -n 1p; else echo "no pandoc on PATH yet"; fi

# news-version (the fleet standard's cheap gates): the top NEWS.md heading is
# either "(development version)" or exactly DESCRIPTION's Version, which
# catches a stale heading left in at release. Ported from seor's
# `news-version` job, with the heading level rurl's NEWS.md uses (`## rurl
# ...`). Pure shell, so it rides in this job instead of taking a runner slot.
gates:
  stage: gates
  script:
    - *gate_deps
    - *pandoc_install
    - 'Rscript tools/verify.R --gates'
    - |
      version="$(grep -E '^Version:' DESCRIPTION | head -n1 | sed -E 's/^Version:[[:space:]]*//')"
      heading="$(grep -m1 -E '^##? ' NEWS.md | sed -E 's/^##?[[:space:]]+(rurl[[:space:]]+)?//')"
      echo "DESCRIPTION Version : '$version'"
      echo "Top NEWS heading    : '$heading'"
      if [ "$heading" = "(development version)" ] || [ "$heading" = "$version" ]; then
        echo "OK: NEWS heading and version are consistent."
      else
        echo "Top NEWS.md heading ('$heading') is neither '(development version)' nor the DESCRIPTION Version ('$version'). Update NEWS.md before release."
        exit 1
      fi

# CITATION.cff `version:` and .zenodo.json `"version"` must name the release
# DESCRIPTION's Version names (X.Y.Z.9000 -> X.Y.Z), and every URL those two
# files declare must also appear in DESCRIPTION's URL: field. Ported from
# seor's `citation-version` job (seor design/adr/0001). No `rules:` here,
# deliberately mirroring `gates` above rather than seor's `.on-mr-and-main`
# anchor, which this file has no equivalent of: `gates` runs on every push the
# top-level `workflow:` block admits (`main` and tags) by omitting `rules:`
# entirely, and this job rides the same default.
#
# `check-bugreports.py` rides along here rather than getting a job of its own
# (SEOR-ocbtrrnl, as in pagerankr): it is stdlib-only, offline and instant,
# with the same shape as check-citation.py, so it belongs in the job that
# already has a python3. A separate job would pay the runner-pickup cost for
# about a second of work.
citation-version:
  stage: gates
  image: python:3.14-alpine
  script:
    - python3 scripts/check-citation.py --self-test
    - python3 scripts/check-citation.py
    - python3 scripts/check-bugreports.py --self-test
    - python3 scripts/check-bugreports.py

# The whole local gate, on every pipeline: `tools/verify.R` runs the manifest
# gates, lint, spelling, `R CMD check --as-cran` through rcmdcheck, failing on
# a WARNING (CRAN incoming feasibility on), and the test suite under LC_ALL=C
# (fleet standard, "CI on every push to main").
#
# ON A TAG, CRAN's version comparison is skipped, and only that. A release tag
# is pushed after CRAN accepts the version, so incoming feasibility then
# compares the tarball against itself on CRAN and reports "Insufficient package
# version" as a WARNING: the v3.1.0 tag pipeline (#209, 2026-10-02) went red
# for exactly that. `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_SKIP_VERSIONS_` turns off that one
# comparison; every other incoming check still runs (ADR 0004 in seor).
check:
  stage: check
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG
      variables:
        _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_SKIP_VERSIONS_: "true"
    - when: on_success
  script:
    # punycoder's configure enables libidn2 when pkg-config finds it, as on
    # CRAN's Debian flavors; its Windows flavors build without it. The two
    # builds can decode differently, and rurl 3.1.0's first upload failed
    # CRAN's Debian pre-test on a probe test that only the libidn2 build broke
    # (RURL-woljcpfu). So this job builds punycoder with libidn2 and says so
    # before the suite runs, and `coverage` asserts the build without it
    # (SEOR-hxxxkmws). r-base ships pkg-config but not libidn2-dev.
    - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libidn2-dev
    - *check_deps
    - *pandoc_install
    - 'Rscript -e ''b <- punycoder:::.backend_info(); print(b); if (!isTRUE(b$has_libidn2)) stop("punycoder was built without libidn2, so this job is not the libidn2 cell (SEOR-hxxxkmws)", call. = FALSE)'''
    # VERIFY_SKIP_DOCS drops verify.R's docs stage here, and only that stage:
    # the `docs-drift` job below runs it instead. The stage needs the roxygen2
    # DESCRIPTION pins, which Debian does not package, and installing it here
    # would pull roxygen2's whole dependency tree from CRAN as source builds
    # into the library this check runs against, shadowing the Debian binaries
    # `.check_deps` installs (SEOR-nwfmerhu). Set inline, not under
    # `variables:`, which tools/local-ci-plan.R does not follow.
    - 'VERIFY_SKIP_DOCS=docs-drift-job Rscript tools/verify.R'

# Generated-docs drift, on every pipeline (SEOR-nwfmerhu): man/ and NAMESPACE
# must match what the roxygen2 that DESCRIPTION pins in
# Config/roxygen2/version regenerates from R/. scripts/check-docs-drift.R
# refuses any other roxygen2, because its output changes between releases,
# and its header says why the check exists at all.
#
# Its own job, not a stage of `check`, because the pinned roxygen2 is
# usually not the current CRAN release and never a Debian package. Here, on
# rocker/r-ver, pak resolves from Posit Package Manager, which serves archived
# versions as binaries too (measured 2026-10-05 in rocker/r-ver:latest on
# arm64: roxygen2 8.0.0 and its whole tree arrived built, nothing compiled,
# in under 30s), into a library no other job uses. The script regenerates in place, which is safe in
# this job's throwaway clone. git is only for the diff it prints on drift.
#
# Self-contained rather than `extends: .rocker`: tools/local-ci-plan.R follows
# no `extends:`, so a template's image and before_script would vanish from a
# local run.
docs-drift:
  stage: check
  needs: []
  image: rocker/r-ver:latest
  script:
    # Every job that runs R on a push installs the pinned pandoc (fleet
    # standard), this one included, though roxygen2 does not call it.
    - *pandoc_install
    - apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git
    - >
      Rscript -e 'if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE))
      install.packages("pak", repos = sprintf(
      "https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/%s/%s/%s",
      .Platform$pkgType, R.Version()$os, R.Version()$arch))'
    - Rscript -e 'pak::pkg_install(c("deps::.", paste0("roxygen2@", read.dcf("DESCRIPTION", "Config/roxygen2/version")[[1]])))'
    - Rscript scripts/check-docs-drift.R

# Coverage, on every pipeline (fleet standard; ADR 0007 in seor). `coverage:`
# feeds the GitLab badge, the cobertura report feeds the merge request diff
# annotations, and the job fails below 95% total coverage. It writes
# cobertura.xml first, so a failing run still annotates. The threshold is
# never lowered: a package under it adds tests. Debian ships covr and xml2 as
# binaries, so the install stays apt-fast like `.check_deps`.
coverage:
  stage: check
  needs: []
  script:
    - *check_deps
    - 'apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends r-cran-covr r-cran-xml2'
    - *pandoc_install
    # The punycoder build without libidn2, as on CRAN's Windows flavors; `check`
    # runs the libidn2 build (SEOR-hxxxkmws).
    - 'Rscript -e ''b <- punycoder:::.backend_info(); print(b); if (!identical(b$has_libidn2, FALSE)) stop("punycoder was built with libidn2, so this job is not the cell without it (SEOR-hxxxkmws)", call. = FALSE)'''
    - >
      Rscript -e 'cov <- covr::package_coverage(quiet = FALSE);
      print(cov);
      covr::to_cobertura(cov);
      pct <- covr::percent_coverage(cov);
      if (pct < 95) stop(sprintf("total coverage %.2f%% is below the fleet minimum of 95%%; add tests, never lower the threshold", pct), call. = FALSE)'
  coverage: '/^rurl Coverage: \d+\.\d+\%/'
  artifacts:
    when: always
    expire_in: 1 week
    reports:
      coverage_report:
        coverage_format: cobertura
        path: cobertura.xml

# The documentation site. Published at https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/rurl/,
# which `_pkgdown.yml` names and DESCRIPTION's `URL:` declares first. Copied
# from pslr's `pages` job (RURL-vkltgopc), with the dependency install swapped
# for this file's apt-based `.check_deps`, which already carries r-cran-pkgdown
# and pandoc.
#
# Every pipeline on `main` deploys it, once `check` has passed (fleet
# standard, "CI on every push to main"), so the site documents `main`. It used
# to deploy only on a tag or a hand-started pipeline, while CI minutes were
# rationed.
#
# The job MUST be named `pages` -- that name is what makes GitLab publish the
# `public/` artifact -- and `tools/local-ci-plan.R` therefore does not treat
# `pages` as a reserved top-level key, so `tools/local-ci.sh --list` shows it.
pages:
  stage: deploy
  needs: ["check"]
  rules:
    # Pinned to the default branch, and that pin is load-bearing. This job
    # does not report on a tree, it PUBLISHES one to
    # <https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/rurl/> for a package that is on CRAN.
    # The `workflow:` block admits a web pipeline on any branch; without the
    # pin, one click on a feature branch would serve unmerged code from the
    # live site with nothing on the page saying so (SEOR-bmgkzhvy).
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
  script:
    - *check_deps
    - *pandoc_install
    # `build_site(install = FALSE)` runs the examples against the INSTALLED
    # package, so install first. This is the same code the tarball would carry.
    - 'R CMD INSTALL --no-multiarch .'
    # pkgdown renders every root-level .md that is not README/NEWS/LICENSE/
    # cran-comments: pkgdown:::package_mds() hardcodes that skip list, so
    # _pkgdown.yml has no setting that can exclude a file. Left alone it
    # publishes whatever top-level .md files exist and folds their text into
    # search.json, where it can outrank real documentation on ordinary
    # queries.
    #
    # KEEP-LIST, NOT DENY-LIST (SEOR-wqxhftpv). This used to name only
    # AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md and move those two out, leaving every other
    # top-level .md file -- named or not -- in place to be published. That is
    # allow-by-default: a new agent-tooling file under any other name (a
    # GEMINI.md, a fresh internal contract) would survive and get published
    # with nothing here noticing, which is how the AGENTS.html/CLAUDE.html
    # leak this job exists to fix reached four sibling repos after being
    # fixed in one. Inverted below: only files on the keep list stay, so an
    # unknown file stays private by default instead of public by default.
    #
    # Keep-list, and why each name is on it:
    #   README.md, NEWS.md, LICENSE.md, cran-comments.md -- pkgdown's own
    #     hardcoded skip list, named here too so this list is a complete,
    #     self-contained claim rather than half of one split between this
    #     file and pkgdown internals.
    #   CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md -- ordinary
    #     user-facing repository docs pkgdown renders as articles.
    #   ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md -- the one per-repo addition: _pkgdown.yml's
    #     navbar names it explicitly (the `acknowledgments` component).
    #   THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md -- not present in this repo today; kept on the
    #     list so adding one later needs no edit here.
    #   ARCHITECTURE.md, RELEASE_NOTES_v1.md -- GRANDFATHERED, deliberately,
    #     not an oversight. Both are already live and indexed --
    #     bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/rurl/{ARCHITECTURE,RELEASE_NOTES_v1}.html
    #     return 200 today and both appear in the published search.json.
    #     SEOR-wqxhftpv exists to stop an UNKNOWN, NEW file from leaking;
    #     retiring a page that is already live and linked is a separate
    #     editorial call, not a side effect of this hygiene fix. Drop them
    #     from this list only as its own deliberate change.
    #
    # Everything else at the top level -- AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and any file
    # added later under any other name -- is moved out, unnamed included.
    #
    # Move rather than delete, still: deleting leaves the search index
    # pointing at pages that 404. This runs after the install so the
    # installed package is byte-identical to a normal build, and the CI
    # checkout is disposable, so nothing is restored after.
    #
    # FAIL LOUD, both directions. README.md, NEWS.md and LICENSE.md are the
    # three pkgdown cannot build a sane site without (no home page, no
    # changelog, a broken license link), so this deliberately fails the job
    # if any of them is missing rather than quietly shipping a half-built
    # site -- the same property the old two-name deny-list had, carried over
    # so a keep-list cannot silently tolerate a vanished README. The other
    # keep-list names are optional: their absence is fine, they simply have
    # nothing to keep.
    #
    # tools/pin-pages-md-filter.R extracts and runs the block between the
    # markers below verbatim against this repo's tracked top-level .md files,
    # so keep the markers on their own lines and keep everything the filter
    # needs (including `set -e` and the mkdir) inside them.
    - |
      # --- agent-md-filter:start ---
      set -e
      mkdir -p /tmp/agent-md
      for req in README.md NEWS.md LICENSE.md; do
        test -f "$req" || { echo "keep-list file missing: $req" >&2; exit 1; }
      done
      for f in *.md; do
        case "$f" in
          README.md|NEWS.md|LICENSE.md|CONTRIBUTING.md|SECURITY.md|CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md|THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md|ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md|cran-comments.md|ARCHITECTURE.md|RELEASE_NOTES_v1.md)
            ;;
          *)
            mv "$f" /tmp/agent-md/
            ;;
        esac
      done
      # --- agent-md-filter:end ---
    # FAVICONS ARE COMMITTED (RURL-ujczpkqm). With a logo in man/figures/ and
    # no pkgdown/favicon/, pkgdown's init_site() calls build_favicons(), which
    # uploads the logo to realfavicongenerator.net -- but only when the CI env
    # var is unset. Here GitLab sets CI=true, so the call was skipped and the
    # site shipped without favicons; `tools/local-ci.sh` sets no CI, so its
    # replay of this job called the API and failed whenever the API did. With
    # pkgdown/favicon/ committed, neither calls out. tools/build-favicons.sh
    # regenerates the set offline after a logo change.
    - 'Rscript -e ''pkgdown::build_site(new_process = FALSE, install = FALSE)'''
    # GitLab Pages publishes `public/`; _pkgdown.yml sets no `destination:`, so
    # the site lands in `docs/` (which .gitignore already covers for local
    # builds). Rename rather than configure, so a local build_site() keeps
    # writing where .gitignore and design/README.md say it does.
    - 'mv docs public'
    - 'test -f public/index.html'
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - public

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# deep-check -- R release, oldrel, devel and the declared floor, on the weekly
# `deep-check` schedule ONLY (fleet standard, "Scheduled pipelines"; schedule
# 4472809 sets SCHEDULE_KIND=deep-check). Both rules halves are required, as
# for the audits below: a job keyed on `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"`
# alone would also fire on the dependency-audit schedule (seor
# design/fleet.md). Schedule-only also keeps `tools/local-ci.sh --all` from
# running them (tools/local-ci-plan.R, schedule_only()).
#
# Copied from punycoder's `full-check` and `floor-check`, the fleet's model:
# rocker/r-ver images, which resolve Posit Package Manager binaries, with
# {pak} installing the dependency tree and its system requirements. The
# `.rocker` template carries punycoder's reasoning in short; read its
# .gitlab-ci.yml for the measurements behind each line. `full-check` installs
# the pinned pandoc from `.pandoc_install`, as the push jobs do.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.rocker:
  image: rocker/r-ver:latest
  interruptible: true
  variables:
    R_LIBS_USER: "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.Rlibs"
    R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: "yes"
    # `--as-cran`'s "checking CRAN incoming feasibility" reads CRAN metadata
    # from the repos option, which rocker points at p3m, and p3m serves none
    # of it: for a package already on CRAN the check halts there and rcmdcheck
    # reads the cut-off log as 0/0/0 (SEOR-ygzjighu). These move only that
    # step to CRAN itself; installs still come from p3m.
    R_CRAN_SRC: "https://cloud.r-project.org"
    R_CRAN_WEB: "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  cache:
    key: "rlibs-$CI_JOB_NAME_SLUG"
    paths:
      - .Rlibs/
  before_script:
    - mkdir -p "$R_LIBS_USER"
    # pak from r-lib's own binary repository: rocker/r-ver:devel has no p3m
    # binaries, and a CRAN source build of pak fails there.
    - >
      Rscript -e 'if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE))
      install.packages("pak", repos = sprintf(
      "https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/%s/%s/%s",
      .Platform$pkgType, R.Version()$os, R.Version()$arch))'
    # rocker's Renviron.site sets R_LIBS, which wins over R_LIBS_USER, so the
    # cache directory is put first on .libPaths() here (SEOR-dyzgzyot).
    - echo '.libPaths(c(Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER"), .libPaths()))' >> "${R_HOME}/etc/Rprofile.site"
    - Rscript -e 'cat("Library paths:\n"); print(.libPaths())'

# R release (`latest`), oldrel (pin the tag to the previous minor when a new R
# minor ships) and devel, each a full `R CMD check --as-cran` with vignettes.
full-check:
  extends: .rocker
  stage: check
  needs: []
  image: $R_IMAGE
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" && $SCHEDULE_KIND == "deep-check"
  parallel:
    matrix:
      - R_IMAGE:
          - "rocker/r-ver:latest"
          - "rocker/r-ver:4.5"
          - "rocker/r-ver:devel"
  script:
    # The three images point `repos` at three shapes: `latest` at p3m
    # `latest`, `4.5` at a FROZEN p3m snapshot (2026-04-23, older than the
    # punycoder and pslr releases DESCRIPTION requires, so pak failed with
    # "Can't find package called punycoder, pslr"; deep-check pipeline
    # 2909433500), and `devel` at cloud.r-project.org. A user .Rprofile, read
    # after Rprofile.site, rewrites a trailing snapshot date to `latest` and
    # puts CRAN itself behind it as a source fallback, because p3m `latest`
    # lags a new CRAN release by up to a day. Testing old R against CURRENT
    # packages is also what CRAN does. Copied from pagerankr's full-check.
    - |
      Rscript -e '
      current <- getOption("repos")[["CRAN"]]
      if (is.null(current) || !nzchar(current) || identical(current, "@CRAN@")) {
        stop("Expected a repo in Rprofile.site, found: ", current, call. = FALSE)
      }
      p3m <- sub("/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$", "/latest", current)
      writeLines(sprintf("options(repos = c(P3M = %s, CRAN = %s))",
                         dQuote(p3m, FALSE),
                         dQuote("https://cloud.r-project.org", FALSE)),
                 file.path(Sys.getenv("HOME"), ".Rprofile"))
      cat("Image pins:", current, "\n  using:", p3m,
          "\n  with CRAN appended as fallback\n")'
    - Rscript -e 'cat("Effective repos:\n"); print(getOption("repos"))'
    - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends qpdf ghostscript
    - *pandoc_install
    - Rscript -e 'pak::pak("deps::.", dependencies = TRUE); pak::pak("any::rcmdcheck")'
    # rcmdcheck reads a check that halted partway as 0/0/0 and returns normally,
    # so error_on never fires; the guard also fails on R CMD check's own exit
    # status (SEOR-maavnxdm).
    - >
      Rscript -e 'res <- rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = c("--no-manual", "--as-cran"),
      build_args = c("--no-manual", "--compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf"),
      error_on = "warning", check_dir = "check");
      if (!identical(as.integer(res$status), 0L)) stop("R CMD check exited with status ", res$status, "; the run did not complete.", call. = FALSE)'
  artifacts:
    when: always
    expire_in: 1 week
    paths:
      - check/

# The leg at the declared R floor, `Depends: R (>= 4.1.0)`. 4.1 is also the
# oldest minor with an arm64 rocker/r-ver image, which the runner needs.
# punycoder's design:
#
# - Packages come from one dated Posit Package Manager snapshot,
#   FLOOR_SNAPSHOT, used in this job alone, so it cannot conflict with what
#   full-check installs. 2025-04-10 is the day before R 4.5.0, when R 4.1 was
#   still inside every dependency's support window.
# - EXCEPT punycoder, pslr and raddr, which first reached CRAN in 2026, after
#   the snapshot, and the rlang (>= 1.1.7) and vctrs (>= 0.7.0) raddr needs,
#   newer than the snapshot's. They come from CRAN itself, as source, with
#   dependencies = FALSE: their own dependencies (Rcpp, cpp11, digest, cli,
#   glue, lifecycle) are already in from the snapshot, so nothing else moves
#   past it. All five declare R >= 4.1 or lower.
# - Only what the check needs: the hard dependencies, the test and vignette
#   Suggests, and rcmdcheck. pkgdown, oysteR and rosv serve the site and the
#   scheduled audits only; the audit tests skip without them, so
#   _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false lets --as-cran report them as a NOTE.
# - Vignettes are neither built nor checked: no pandoc here, and the tests
#   exercise the same functions.
floor-check:
  extends: .rocker
  stage: check
  needs: []
  image: rocker/r-ver:4.1.3
  variables:
    FLOOR_SNAPSHOT: "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2025-04-10"
    _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_: "false"
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" && $SCHEDULE_KIND == "deep-check"
  script:
    - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends pkg-config libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev libicu-dev
    - >
      Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("Rcpp", "cpp11", "digest", "cli", "glue", "lifecycle", "stringi", "testthat", "withr", "jsonlite", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "rcmdcheck"),
      repos = Sys.getenv("FLOOR_SNAPSHOT"), Ncpus = 4L);
      install.packages(c("rlang", "vctrs", "raddr", "punycoder", "pslr"), repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org", dependencies = FALSE);
      stopifnot(all(vapply(c("stringi", "punycoder", "pslr", "raddr", "testthat", "withr", "rcmdcheck"), requireNamespace, NA, quietly = TRUE)));
      print(R.version.string)'
    # rcmdcheck reads a check that halted partway as 0/0/0 and returns normally,
    # so error_on never fires; the guard also fails on R CMD check's own exit
    # status (SEOR-maavnxdm).
    - >
      Rscript -e 'res <- rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = c("--no-manual", "--as-cran", "--ignore-vignettes"),
      build_args = c("--no-manual", "--no-build-vignettes"),
      error_on = "warning", check_dir = "check");
      if (!identical(as.integer(res$status), 0L)) stop("R CMD check exited with status ", res$status, "; the run did not complete.", call. = FALSE)'
  artifacts:
    when: always
    expire_in: 1 week
    paths:
      - check/

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# fossa -- the FOSSA license and security scan, on every push to `main`
# (fleet standard, "FOSSA": rurl holds one of the five free-plan slots).
#
# `fossa analyze` uploads to the project `.fossa.yml` names,
# git+gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/rurl; the first run creates it, and the README's
# FOSSA badges read "not found" until then. It reads `FOSSA_API_KEY`, a masked
# CI/CD variable only the owner can set. The CLI comes from FOSSA's official
# install script, which picks the linux/arm64 build on this runner. Plain and
# blocking, like every other job: an unreachable FOSSA turns the pipeline red.
# Push only, so a schedule or a hand-started pipeline does not re-upload.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fossa:
  stage: audit
  image: debian:stable-slim
  needs: []
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "push" && $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
  script:
    - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates git
    - 'curl -fsSL -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fossas/fossa-cli/master/install-latest.sh | bash'
    - fossa analyze

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# audit -- the two dependency-vulnerability audits, UNATTENDED, and nothing else
# (SEOR-fftbjnpl).
#
# WHY THEY ARE HERE. tests/testthat/test-osv.R (OSV via {rosv}) and
# test-security.R (Sonatype OSS Index via {oysteR}) are advisory audits: their
# answer is a fact about the world, not about the tree, so they were taken out
# of the pre-push gate's test cell (tools/verify.R filters `security|osv` out
# of its test_local() run; leave that filter alone). That left nothing running
# them at all: the GitHub workflows that did were deleted with RURL-vunvxusf,
# and `check`'s own test run never reached them either (R CMD check leaves
# NOT_CRAN unset, so both skip_on_cran()). These two jobs are the unattended
# run.
#
# ONLY A PIPELINE SCHEDULE CARRYING THE SELECTOR STARTS THEM. The rule needs
# both `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"` and `$SCHEDULE_KIND ==
# "dependency-audit"`, then `when: never`, so a push to `main`, a tag, a
# hand-started pipeline and any other schedule never pay for them. The
# `workflow:` block above admits a scheduled pipeline because a schedule runs
# on `main` and `$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH` holds there; the
# jobs without `rules:` (`gates`, `citation-version`, `check`, `coverage`) and
# `pages` ride along in that pipeline too.
#
# OWNER GATE, not settable from a merge request: create the schedule under
# Build > Pipeline schedules, target `main`, with the variable
# SCHEDULE_KIND=dependency-audit; and set the OSS Index CI/CD variables
#   OSSINDEX_USER   - the literal placeholder `x`, NOT the account email
#   OSSINDEX_TOKEN  - a Sonatype Guide personal access token (masked)
# Until the schedule exists neither job runs.
#
# OSS Index moved to Sonatype Guide, whose help says the basic-auth username is
# ignored for a PAT. It is not: with the account email as username a valid PAT
# returns HTTP 401, and with `x` the same token returns 200 (measured in
# pagerankr 2026-07-25 by changing only OSSINDEX_USER). A local
# `curl -u "x:$PAT"` that succeeds while `security-audit` 401s is this, not a
# bad token. A legacy OSS Index API token, if one is ever rotated back in, is
# the case that takes the email.
#
# BOTH INSTALL rurl FIRST, and that is load-bearing. test-osv.R resolves
# rurl's runtime closure from installed.packages(); against an uninstalled
# rurl the closure is empty and the test skips "no resolvable runtime
# dependencies" -- a green job that audited nothing. test-security.R audits
# the DESCRIPTION that system.file() resolves. Installing makes both read what
# a user installs.
#
# The dependency install mirrors `.check_deps`: Debian binaries where they
# exist, CRAN for the rest, then an assertion, because install.packages()
# reports a failed install as a warning and exits 0.
#
# `tools/local-ci-plan.R --all` deliberately leaves these two out: they need
# the network and forge-held credentials, and a post-merge local run is not
# the place a new upstream advisory should turn red.
.audit_deps: &audit_deps
  - apt-get update -qq
  - 'apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends
     r-cran-stringi r-cran-testthat r-cran-pkgload r-cran-withr r-cran-jsonlite
     r-cran-curl r-cran-httr'
  - 'Rscript -e ''install.packages(c("rlang", "vctrs", "raddr", "punycoder", "pslr", "rosv", "oysteR"))'''
  - 'Rscript -e ''p <- c("raddr", "punycoder", "pslr", "testthat", "pkgload", "rosv", "oysteR"); m <- p[!vapply(p, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]; if (length(m)) stop("missing dependencies: ", paste(m, collapse = ", "))'''
  - 'R CMD INSTALL --no-multiarch .'

osv-audit:
  stage: audit
  needs: []
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" && $SCHEDULE_KIND == "dependency-audit"
    - when: never
  variables:
    # testthat::test_local() sets NOT_CRAN=true itself; explicit anyway, so
    # skip_on_cran() cannot silently turn the audit into a skip.
    NOT_CRAN: "true"
  script:
    - *audit_deps
    - 'Rscript -e ''testthat::test_local(filter = "^osv$", stop_on_failure = TRUE)'''

# OSSINDEX_AUDIT_REQUIRED turns every missing precondition in
# test-security.R (oysteR absent, OSSINDEX_USER / OSSINDEX_TOKEN absent) into
# a failure instead of a skip. It is set here and nowhere else, so local runs
# and `R CMD check` still skip.
security-audit:
  stage: audit
  needs: []
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" && $SCHEDULE_KIND == "dependency-audit"
    - when: never
  variables:
    NOT_CRAN: "true"
    OSSINDEX_AUDIT_REQUIRED: "true"
  script:
    - *audit_deps
    - 'Rscript -e ''testthat::test_local(filter = "^security$", stop_on_failure = TRUE)'''
